input.findings: Initial submission for review. No findings yet.

Parent investigation (attributed, to be independently validated): The candidate client adds an unconditional post-save receipt check requiring response["applied"] is True. The supported released provider at eval-release returns {"ok": True} with no `applied` key and ignores `require_receipt`. Therefore ordinary saves (enhanced_settings=False, the default and the disabled-UI case) against the released provider now raise RuntimeError although the provider persisted the values — a regression against the explicit delivery contract that ordinary saves must keep working with the eval-release provider and that main stays independently releasable. The receipt check is not gated on enhanced_settings. The updated unit test returns a mock {"ok": True, "applied": True}, encoding pending Task-2 provider behavior, so the passing test does not exercise and cannot catch the released-provider incompatibility. Candidate provider is not deployed and cannot serve as the baseline. Provisional severity: critical/P0 compatibility + data-integrity (caller sees failure after a successful persist; retries are non-idempotent at the client contract level).
